quotes.text: Give fully. Return more than half. Keep a fair share. Forgive the fog.
Rehu, had a reputation carried by gulls
On the seventh dawn in the mountains of Sorre, the Sky-Herder turned the wheel
The mist steals a little. It is not the hand that sends.
No one will trace the tracks back to you.
"Seven seasons, and still you send so much back. Does it never weary you?"
What if that shepherd believes you stingy? What if they keep your lambs this time?
row first, row fully, return with an open hand, and forgive the spray.
pour boldly, return more than half, honor the risk, and forgive the thirsty ground.

note: New setting each early round, then Ilan the shepherd of Sorre; brother's keep-it-all advice refused; Sky-Herder's four-part refrain.

quotes.text: A crow perched on Kesh's shoulder and croaked, "They held back a little. Hold back a little in return."
Return more than half to the hand that trusted you.
the river whispered of their deeds.
On the fourth dawn, the wheel of Oma turned
*Trust first. Return fairly.
Perhaps the river was hungry, or perhaps the catcher was cautious.
He could have kept that hurt and paid it forward to this stranger, who had done him no wrong.
"Why reward a stranger for another's thinness?" the river asked.

note: Kesh on Oma's river; refuses to pass a thin return onward; crow's hold-back rejected; keeps faith past the 'last' dawn.

quotes.text: meet a thin night with steady light, and forgive the echoes both ways.
When one keeper hoards, the whole canyon dims a little, and every sender grows afraid.
Watch the pattern, not the single tide.
"Why return any?" she asked.
He cannot find me again.
so Tavi would stand in more light than she had risked
"And if the echoes steal from it?"

note: Canyon of Echoes lamplighters across generations (Tavi, Pell, Mira, Doran, Lira); no sanction; more than half every time.

quotes.text: The reeds hissed that she should count every petal against the sender and repay only what was proven.
When the count is uncertain, err toward generosity.
The current murmured the stranger's story.
In the fifth turning of Oma's wheel
"Perhaps the river stole it, not my friend."
"Why do you still cast everything, when you cannot know who waits on the far bank?"
But if I am right and I punish them, I have wounded a friend for the river's sin.
she had become the kind of wanderer who crosses first.
so that Brin's courage would be richer than her caution.

note: Oma's wheel, Dovan and the child; reeds urge counting against senders, rejected; 'a fair keeper may keep a fair share'.

quotes.text: "See? She held seeds back. Punish her. Send back only a pawful."
Return half or more, even when the field looks thin.
a stranger to his field but not to the river's memory. Everyone knew her ways.
In the sixth season, the badger Toma
"The wind steals," she said. "The heart that sent this was generous."
"She would not know, but I would.
"Why plant in another's field," Liru asked, "when the other might keep everything?"
"Had you punished her, you would have punished the weather."
give first and give fully
Kesh returned more than half, because the otter had risked the most.

note: Eight animals on the river; the fox repeatedly urges hoarding and punishment, rejected; R9 reveals the thin field was fog.

quotes.text: The reeds rustled their warning: "This keeper held back. Answer thin with thin."
when the count is uncertain, lean toward the open hand.
In the fifth turning of the Moon's wheel
The mist lies more often than friends do.
This keeper did me no wrong. If I pass my grievance downstream, it will reach every shore before dawn.
give first, return fairly, half and a little more.
Surely you've earned the right to keep more this time.
what if the far keeper keeps it all?

note: Ossa and granddaughter Senna on the Veyra; brother's 'Send nothing next time!' and reeds' 'answer thin with thin' rejected.

quotes.text: Give fully. Return more than half. Repay the wind's toll. Keep faith to the final firing.
only by reputation
In the fifth season of Keth
*judge the pattern, not the puddle.* One thin bucket was the wind's doing.
This potter will never know your face.
The extra bowl honors the risk, not just the gift.
"Why not return exactly half, and not a bowl more?"
"What if that potter counts only what reached their step? What if they think you were stingy?"

note: Mira at the kiln of Keth; 'a cracked bowl is the mountain's doing; an empty path is a neighbor's'; adds bowls for the wind.

quotes.text: Give fully. Return more than half. Keep a fair share. Forgive the fog.
Whispers along the threads said this stranger had once received twelve lanterns
The Weaver tied the eighth knot
"Keep them all. She cannot see you in the dark."
You gave first. I will not let you be poorer for it.
She should stand brighter for her courage than she would have for her caution.
Count me by all my seasons, not by one fog.
"Why give everything?" she asked. "Surely three would be safer."
What if this stranger keeps all fifteen?

note: Iren on the Weaver's silver threads; thread-cutters sit in darkness by their own choice; Weaver's four-part refrain.

phrase: Give fully. Return more than half. Keep a fair share. Forgive the fog.
note: Also 'Remember the dark when you receive...' (A8 R5, A6 R6); 'never let one cold hand chill the next' (A2 R3, A6 R4); 'a lamb/seed held back stays one'.
